(11 October 2026) | attendance = 37,274 | average attendance = 6,212 | prevseason = [[2025–26 Indian Super League|2025–26]] | nextseason = [[2027–28 Indian Super League|2027-28]] | updated = 16 October 2026 }} The '''2026–27 Indian Super League''', also known as the '''MG Indian Super League''' (due to sponsorship reasons with [[JSW MG Motor India|MG Motor]]), is the 13th season of the [[Indian Super League]] (ISL) and the 31st season of top-tier [[Indian football league system|Indian football]]. The season began on 10 October 2026. [[Sony Sports Network|Sony Sports]] and [[Google]] have acquired the league's media rights for the next two seasons. Sony Sports holds the satellite television rights for the Indian subcontinent, and streams matches on [[SonyLIV]] in India, while Google streams every match live on [[YouTube]] in India and worldwide. [[East Bengal FC|East Bengal]] are the defending champions, having won their maiden Super League title and their fourth overall top-tier league title. == Developments == === March === * On 2 March 2026, the [[All India Football Federation]] (AIFF) invited bids for the commercial rights to its men's and women's club competitions for a minimum term of 15 years beginning with the [[2026–27 in Indian football|2026–27 season]]. The tender covered media, digital, data, sponsorship and other commercial assets attached to the [[Indian Super League]] (ISL) and [[AIFF Super Cup|Federation Cup]], and was structured as a 15-year agreement with an optional five-year extension, a right of first refusal for the successful bidder and a five per cent annual increase in value.{{Cite web |date=27 March 2026 |title=AIFF opens bids for RFP for commercial rights of club competitions |url=https://www.the-aiff.com/article/aiff-opens-bids-for-commercial-rights-of-club-competitions |publisher=All India Football Federation |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=28 March 2026 |title=ISL clubs urge AIFF to pause binding rights decision at ExCo meet |work=Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/sports/football-news/isl-clubs-urge-aiff-to-pause-binding-rights-decision-at-exco-meet-126032800881_1.html |access-date=3 August 2026}} * Three companies submitted bids. London-based [[Genius Sports]] and [[FanCode]] bid for the ISL and Federation Cup package.{{Cite news |last=Negi |first=Ashish |date=26 March 2026 |title=Excl: AIFF receives three bids, including Genius Sports, for ISL & IWL long-term rights tender |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-isl-iwl-tender-fancode-genius-sports-capri-sports |access-date=3 August 2026}} * On 27 March 2026, the AIFF opened the technical bids in the morning and the commercial bids later the same day. Genius Sports emerged as the highest bidder for the men's package at approximately {{INRConvert|64.39|c}} per year, or about {{INRConvert|2129|c}} across 20 years, while FanCode offered {{INRConvert|36|c}} in the first year, amounting to roughly {{INRConvert|1190|c}} over the same period. The figures marked a sharp rise on the existing cycle, in which FanCode had acquired the [[2025–26 Indian Super League|2025–26]] ISL media rights for {{INRConvert|8.62|c}} and production costs had left the federation with net revenue of about {{INRConvert|3.4|c}}.{{Cite news |last=Lakhina |first=Tanuj |date=28 March 2026 |title=Explained: Why ISL clubs want FanCode over Genius Sports as commercial partner |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/why-isl-clubs-want-fancode-over-genius-sports-as-commercial-partner-explained/articleshow/129864373.cms |issn=0971-8257 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |last=Negi |first=Ashish |date=27 March 2026 |title=Genius Sports bids highest for ISL; Capri Sports leads IWL commercial race |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-isl-genius-sports-capri-sports-iwl-rights |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=29 March 2026 |title=₹2,129 crore on the table, but why do ISL clubs still see the Genius Sports bid as a problem? |work=The Bridge |url=https://thebridge.in/football/aiff-commercial-rights-tender-genius-sports-isl-56213 |access-date=3 August 2026}} * Under the model set out in the tender, the AIFF was to receive a fifth of the committed annual spend in advance, with 70 per cent of net revenue shared with the federation at the end of each season and 60 per cent of that sum distributed among the participating clubs. The two bids divided the stakeholders: the federation favoured Genius Sports for its larger guaranteed payments, while the clubs preferred FanCode's lower upfront commitment, which they argued left more scope for central revenue to reach them. * On 28 March 2026, the ISL clubs wrote jointly to the AIFF asking it not to take a binding decision at the Executive Committee meeting scheduled for the following day, stating that the tender documents had been made available less than 12 hours before the bids were opened and seeking detailed presentations from both bidders.{{Cite news |date=28 March 2026 |title=ISL clubs seek more time as AIFF weighs bids for 20-year commercial deal |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-clubs-seek-more-time-as-aiff-weighs-bids-isl-commercial-tender-202603 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=28 March 2026 |title=AIFF receives ISL rights bids worth over ₹2,000 crore; decision expected on 29 March |work=The Indian Express |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/football/aiff-receives-isl-rights-bids-rs-2000-crore-march-29-decision-10605348/ |access-date=3 August 2026}} === May === * On 14 May 2026, the ISL clubs proposed that they take over the commercial running of the league themselves under a club-led model. The AIFF did not accept the proposal outright at that stage.{{Cite news |last=Lakhina |first=Tanuj |date=8 July 2026 |title=AIFF, ISL teams bury the hatchet, ink four-year deal towards club-led model |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/news/aiff-isl-teams-bury-the-hatchet-ink-four-year-deal-towards-club-led-model/articleshow/132259983.cms |access-date=3 August 2026}} * On 17 May 2026, the AIFF Club Licensing Committee–First Instance Body granted the Premier 1 licence, with sanctions, to seven clubs — [[NorthEast United FC|NorthEast United]], [[East Bengal FC|East Bengal]], [[Jamshedpur FC|Jamshedpur]], [[Mumbai City FC|Mumbai City]], [[Bengaluru FC|Bengaluru]], [[FC Goa|Goa]] and [[Punjab FC|Punjab]]. The applications of [[SC Delhi]], [[Odisha FC|Odisha]], [[Mohun Bagan Super Giant]], [[Chennaiyin FC|Chennaiyin]], [[Kerala Blasters FC|Kerala Blasters]], [[Mohammedan SC (Kolkata)|Mohammedan]] and [[Inter Kashi FC|Inter Kashi]] were rejected.{{Cite news |date=20 May 2026 |title=Seven ISL clubs, including East Bengal, granted Premier 1 licence; Mohun Bagan among seven rejected |work=Deccan Herald |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/sports/football/seven-isl-clubs-including-east-bengal-granted-premier-1-licence-mohun-bagan-among-seven-rejected-4010288 |access-date=3 August 2026}} * On 23 May 2026, the Genius Sports bid for the league's commercial rights could not be approved at a Special General Meeting in [[Kolkata]] after several clubs sought greater clarity on the associated revenue-sharing model. * Following the meeting, the AIFF set 15 June 2026 as the deadline for clubs to confirm participation for the 2026–27 season with a {{INRConvert|1|c}} fee. The federation also outlined plans to begin the 2026–27 season with the [[Durand Cup]] in July before starting a 14-team double [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] league by early September. The clubs presented a counter-proposal promising to generate approximately {{INRConvert|60|c}} annually to operate the league and cup competitions while matching most of the commitments made by Genius Sports, which had offered {{INRConvert|67|c}} annually for 15+5 years. === June === * By early June 2026, with the calendar still unresolved, more than 150 ISL players were out of contract, several of them internationals, and most clubs had not opened renewal talks. [[Óscar Bruzón]] left East Bengal shortly after guiding the club to its first national league title in 22 years, while Goa and East Bengal, both due to appear in AFC competitions, were unable to begin preparations.{{Cite news |last=Giri |first=Rahul |date=2 June 2026 |title=ISL clubs raise offer to acquire league's commercial rights amid growing uncertainty |work=RevSportz |url=https://revsportz.in/isl-clubs-raise-offer-to-acquire-leagues-commercial-rights-amid-growing-uncertainty/ |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=1 June 2026 |title=ISL player contracts expire amid uncertainty |work=Rediff |url=https://www.rediff.com/sports/report/isl-player-contracts-expire-amid-uncertainty/20260601.htm |access-date=3 August 2026}} * In early June 2026, following meetings between club owners in [[Mumbai]], the clubs emailed AIFF deputy secretary general M. Satyanarayan a revised proposal for a two-year club-led pilot model under which the federation would receive {{INRConvert|15|c}} annually for the league's commercial rights.{{Cite news |last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=3 June 2026 |title=ISL clubs propose new 2-year pilot model, refuse entry fee of Rs 1 crore |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/isl-clubs-propose-new-2-year-pilot-model-refuse-entry-fee-of-rs-1-crore/articleshow/131470531.cms |access-date=3 August 2026}} * The proposal exceeded the approximately {{INRConvert|12.4|c}} that Genius Sports had committed as administrative fees for the 2026–27 season. Writing on behalf of the clubs, [[FC Goa]] chief executive Ravi Puskur argued that prevailing market conditions undervalued the league and that none of the clubs would pay the proposed {{INRConvert|1|c}} participation fee under a Genius Sports-led commercial model. * On 8 June 2026, Union Sports Minister [[Mansukh Mandaviya]] met AIFF officials, club representatives and former AIFF president [[Praful Patel]] at the [[Sports Authority of India]] office in New Delhi. He assured the clubs that the 2026–27 season would proceed as scheduled and asked both sides to establish a task force to prepare a structured roadmap for the league.{{Cite news |date=9 June 2026 |title=AIFF agrees "in principle" to two-year club-led model of ISL; 2026–27 season to start on Sep 4 |work=Deccan Chronicle |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/sports/aiff-agrees-in-principle-to-two-year-club-led-model-of-isl-2026-27-season-to-start-on-sep-4-1962428 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=9 June 2026 |title=ISL clubs push club-led model, offer AIFF higher revenue share |work=O Heraldo |url=https://www.heraldgoa.in/goa/isl-clubs-push-club-led-model-offer-aiff-higher-revenue-share/477515/ |access-date=3 August 2026}} * The meeting resulted in a four-year club-led proposal under which each of the 14 clubs would contribute {{INRConvert|1.1|c}} annually, generating {{INRConvert|15.4|c}} in administration fees for the AIFF. On 9 June, the federation announced that it had agreed to the proposal in principle, with the season expected to begin on 4 September while the Durand Cup would run from 25 June to 25 July. * On 20 June 2026, an AIFF Special General Meeting approved a proposal permitting clubs in the ISL and the [[Indian Football League]] (IFL) to field a starting eleven containing three foreign players and one player holding [[Overseas Citizenship of India]] (OCI). At least 12 of the 14 clubs opposed the measure, while Mohun Bagan Super Giant later submitted recommendations including making OCI selection optional and limiting registrations.{{Cite news |date=21 June 2026 |title=ISL clubs apprehensive of AIFF's proposal on OCI/PIO quota |work=News9 |url=https://www.news9live.com/sports/football/isl-clubs-apprehensive-of-aiffs-proposal-on-oci-pio-quota-2982227 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=29 June 2026 |title=Mohun Bagan propose roadmap for OCI players, submit detailed recommendations to AIFF |work=RevSportz |url=https://revsportz.in/mohun-bagan-propose-roadmap-for-oci-players-submit-detailed-recommendations-to-aiff/ |access-date=3 August 2026}} === July === * On 2 July 2026, after accepting the clubs' proposal in principle, the AIFF sought clarification on three provisions before formally transferring the league's commercial rights: audit rights over the ISL special purpose vehicle, a 10% share of the league's net profits, and the clubs' right to terminate the agreement after two years.{{Cite news |last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=2 July 2026 |title=AIFF seeks clarity on three clauses before inking deal with ISL clubs |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/aiff-seeks-clarity-on-three-clauses-before-inking-deal-with-isl-clubs/articleshow/132144925.cms |access-date=3 August 2026}} * The AIFF instead proposed a renegotiation mechanism after two seasons, with any termination requiring sufficient notice to allow alternative arrangements for the league's continued operation. * On 8 July 2026, the AIFF and the ISL Managing Committee formally signed a four-year club-led agreement after resolving outstanding issues relating to independent auditing, profit-sharing and the termination clause.{{Cite web |date=8 July 2026 |title=AIFF, ISL clubs outline club-led commercial model for Indian Super League |url=https://www.the-aiff.com/article/aiff-isl-clubs-outline-club-led-commercial-model-for-indian-super-league |publisher=All India Football Federation |access-date=3 August 2026}} * Under the agreement, clubs would hold the league's commercial rights through a special purpose vehicle while the AIFF retained regulatory control. Participation fees were fixed at {{INRConvert|1.1|c}}, {{INRConvert|1.15|c}}, {{INRConvert|1.2|c}} and {{INRConvert|1.25|c}} over four seasons, with promotion and relegation continuing and the league reverting to a full home-and-away format. * In mid-July 2026, Satyanarayan wrote to all 14 clubs requiring written confirmation of participation together with the first instalment of {{INRConvert|55|l}} by 20 July, with the second {{INRConvert|55|l}} due before 14 August.{{Cite news |date=10 July 2026 |title=How much are clubs paying AIFF for ISL 2026–27? Participation fee, deadlines revealed |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-isl-2026-27-participation-fee-deadlines-revealed |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=10 July 2026 |title=AIFF has asked all 14 clubs to confirm participation and pay the first instalment of ₹55 lakh by July 20 |work=RevSportz |url=https://revsportz.in/aiff-has-asked-all-14-clubs-to-confirm-participation-and-pay-the-first-instalment-of-%E2%82%B955-lakh-by-july-20/ |access-date=3 August 2026}} * By the 20 July 2026 deadline, 12 of the 14 clubs had completed the first instalment, with [[Jamshedpur FC|Jamshedpur]] and [[Inter Kashi FC|Inter Kashi]] the only two outstanding; both had written to the AIFF seeking an extension on operational grounds. The first instalments of East Bengal, Mohun Bagan SG and Diamond Harbour were adjusted against prize money owed to them from the previous season.{{Cite news |date=21 July 2026 |title=Excl: 12 ISL clubs pay first installment of participation fee; Jamshedpur FC & Inter Kashi yet to comply |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/isl-2026-27-aiff-first-installement-participation-fees |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{Cite news |date=21 July 2026 |title=ISL participation: Jamshedpur FC seek more time |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/isl-participation-jamshedpur-fc-seek-more-time/articleshow/132550515.cms |access-date=3 August 2026}} * On 25 July 2026, the AIFF, together with the clubs, released a [[Request for proposal|Request for Proposal]] (RFP) for the media rights of the season under the new club-led commercial model. The RFP offered two packages: Package A combined media rights with live production responsibilities, while Package B offered media rights without production, with the clubs responsible for arranging live production.{{Cite news |last=Chatterjee |first=Triyasha |date=25 July 2026 |title=AIFF releases RFP for ISL 2026-27 media rights |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-aiff-rfp-isl-26-27-media-rights |access-date=20 August 2026}} * On 31 July 2026, the league signed a new four-year agreement with Swiss sports technology company [[Sportradar]] to remain the league's official Data and Integrity Partner until the end of the 2029–30 season. The agreement was valued at {{INRConvert|57|c}}, equivalent to {{INRConvert|15|c}} per season, representing an increase of approximately 21% over the previous full-season agreement for the [[2024–25 Indian Super League|2024–25 season]].{{Cite news |last=Negi |first=Ashish |date=31 July 2026 |title=Exclusive: ISL & Sportradar sign new four-year deal worth over ₹57 crore |url=https://khelnow.com/football/isl-sportradar-new-four-year-deal |work=Khel Now |access-date=31 July 2026}} * On 31 July 2026, [[Jamshedpur FC|Jamshedpur]] announced that it would not participate in the 2026–27 season, ending its nine-year association with the competition after being a member since the [[2017–18 Indian Super League|2017–18 season]]. The club had failed to pay the {{INRConvert|55|l}} participation fee by the extended deadline after previously seeking additional time to complete internal shareholder approval procedures. [[Inter Kashi]] paid its instalment on the same day. The withdrawal reduced the number of participating clubs from 14 to 13 for the 2026–27 season.{{Cite web |date=31 July 2026 |title=Jamshedpur Football Club statement |url=https://x.com/JamshedpurFC/status/2083198029017088360 |publisher=Jamshedpur FC |access-date=31 July 2026}}{{Cite news |last=Bose |first=Shuvaditya |date=31 July 2026 |title='Devastated, didn't see this coming:' Players stunned as Jamshedpur FC quits ISL |work=The Indian Express |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/football/jamshedpur-fc-quits-isl-players-stunned-devastated-10812492/ |access-date=31 July 2026}}{{Cite news |last=Lakhina |first=Tanuj |date=31 July 2026 |title=Jamshedpur FC pulls out of ISL after missing participation deadline |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/isl-jamshedpur-fc-pull-out-of-2026-27-season-inter-kashi-pay-rs-55-lakh-participation-fees |access-date=31 July 2026}} === August === * On 13 August 2026, the Indian Super League secured a new two-year agreement with [[Nivia Sports]], which retained its position as the league's official ball and equipment partner from the 2026–27 season. Nivia will supply official match balls to the league and its participating clubs, as well as referee kits and apparel for the league's central team.{{Cite web |last=Negi |first=Ashish |date=13 August 2026 |title=Nivia retains ISL ball rights after beating competition from two foreign brands |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-nivia-sports-isl-new-deal-official-ball-partner |website=Khel Now |access-date=16 August 2026}} * On 14 August 2026, [[Tata Steel]] agreed to transfer its entire equity stake in Jamshedpur Football and Sporting Private Limited (JFSPL) to [[Churchill Brothers FC|Churchill Brothers]] for a token consideration of {{INRConvert|100}}. The agreement included the transfer of Jamshedpur FC's league sporting licence and the contracts of 12 players and two coaches. Churchill Brothers agreed to take over the contracts of players and coaching staff from September 2026, subject to AIFF approval and other applicable conditions.{{Cite press release |date=14 August 2026 |title=Tata Steel transfers ownership of Jamshedpur Football & Sporting Pvt. Ltd. to Churchill Brothers FC |url=https://www.tatasteel.com/newsroom/press-releases/india/2026/tata-steel-transfers-ownership-of-jamshedpur-football-sporting-pvt-ltd-to-churchill-brothers-fc/ |publisher=Tata Steel |access-date=16 August 2026}}{{Cite web |last=Chatterjee |first=Triyasha |date=14 August 2026 |title=13 clubs complete second instalment of participation fee for ISL 2026-27 |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-13-clubs-second-instalment-participation-fee-for-isl-2026-27 |website=Khel Now |access-date=16 August 2026}} * On 14 August 2026, 13 of the 14 participating clubs completed the second instalment of the ISL participation fee for the 2026–27 season. [[Churchill Brothers FC|Churchill Brothers]], following its agreement to acquire Jamshedpur FC's sporting licence and the ownership of JFSPL, also completed the full participation fee payment. [[Diamond Harbour FC|Diamond Harbour]] were the only club yet to make the second payment. * On 18 August 2026, [[Diamond Harbour FC|Diamond Harbour]] sought additional time from the AIFF to clear its outstanding final instalment of the ISL participation fee and confirm its participation in the 2026–27 season. The AIFF had set 14 August as the deadline for clubs to complete the {{INRConvert|1.1|c}} participation fee in two instalments of {{INRConvert|55|l}} each.{{Cite news |last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=18 August 2026 |title=Diamond Harbour seek more time, AIFF unlikely to wait long |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/diamond-harbour-seek-more-time-aiff-unlikely-to-wait-long/articleshow/133305081.cms |access-date=18 August 2026}} * On 19 August 2026, the AIFF, on behalf of the federation and the participating clubs, confirmed that the season would proceed with 13 clubs after [[Diamond Harbour FC|Diamond Habour]] failed to complete its outstanding participation-fee payment by the extended deadline. The season will be played in a double [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] format on a home-and-away basis. * On 19 August 2026, the clubs opened direct discussions with [[Zee Entertainment Enterprises|Zee]] and [[Sony Sports Network|Sony Sports]] over the league's media rights for the upcoming four-season cycle after the tender attracted only one bid. [[Google]] also held discussions with the clubs regarding potential support for making the matches available live on [[YouTube]].{{Cite news |last=Sharma |first=Ayushman |date=19 August 2026 |title=Zee & Sony Sports in direct talks with ISL clubs over media rights |work=Khel Now |url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-isl-clubs-zee-sony-media-right |access-date=20 August 2026}} * On 22 August 2026, the AIFF was reported to be considering a one-season suspension of relegation from the league following the reduction in participating clubs from 14 to 13, subject to approval from the league governing council and the executive committee. [[Diamond Harbour FC]]'s failure to complete its participation-fee payment left the league with 13 teams, while [[Mohammedan SC (Kolkata)|Mohammedan]] had already been relegated after finishing bottom of the previous season.{{Cite news |last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=22 August 2026 |title=With reduced teams, AIFF likely to freeze relegation in ISL this season |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/with-reduced-teams-aiff-likely-to-freeze-relegation-in-isl-this-season/articleshow/133412405.cms |access-date=22 August 2026}} === September === * On 2 September 2026, the AIFF informed the clubs that relegation would continue to apply at the conclusion of the 2026–27 season despite the reduction in participating clubs from 14 to 13. [[Diamond Harbour FC]], which had won the [[Indian Football League|IFL]] in 2025–26 and earned promotion to the ISL, did not take up its promoted slot. The AIFF therefore ruled that they would be deemed to finish at the bottom of the table, would not be eligible to earn points during the season, and would not retain ISL status for 2027–28, meaning the club would compete in the IFL in that season.{{Cite news |last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=2 September 2026 |title=AIFF confirms no relegation in ISL, Diamond Harbour set to go down |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/aiff-confirms-no-relegation-in-isl-diamond-harbour-set-to-go-down/articleshow/133690371.cms |access-date=3 September 2026}} * The AIFF also confirmed the return of the [[Indian Super League]] playoff system, with six teams competing for the league championship.{{Cite news |last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=2 September 2026 |title=AIFF confirms no relegation in ISL, Diamond Harbour set to go down |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/aiff-confirms-no-relegation-in-isl-diamond-harbour-set-to-go-down/articleshow/133690371.cms |access-date=3 September 2026}} * On 29 September 2026, the UAE-based sports consortium [[Al Fursan Group]] signed a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of [[Kerala Blasters FC]] from [[Magnum Sports]]. The ownership transfer is to be completed in phases over eight months, subject to regulatory and league requirements. The transaction was reportedly valued at around {{INRConvert|120|c}}.
